quests.title: Returns at Wiley Park
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. I am sending back 84 papers a day from Wiley Park and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: the returns stack, at its worst
the distributor needs to see the size of it

quests.title: The Better Rate, Wiley Park
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. They will drop my Wiley Park order if I can show $45 of turnover on the other side of the shop by grand final week. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: $45, and cards and stationery count
sell anything, I am not proud

quests.title: The Wiley Park Round
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. I do the Wiley Park round from half six and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the end of the round, where it starts
whoever is on that street at that hour

quests.title: The Dog on Ash Street, Wiley Park
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. There is a dog on the Wiley Park round that has had two of my bags and two hundred metres of orange netting that was not even mine. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: you will want your wits about you
the owner, not the dog, I am not a monster
tell me it is sorted

quests.title: The Syndicate, Wiley Park
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. Nine of us at Wiley Park have gone in on the same numbers since grand final week and one of us has stopped putting money in. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: the house of the one who stopped
$84, which is his share since he stopped
I want it said out loud, not in the group chat

quests.title: The Other Agency, Wiley Park
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. The agency at Punchbowl closed six months before Wiley Park started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

steps.label: the shop is shut, the family is not
whatever they say, say it slowly to me

quests.title: The Unclaimed Falcon, Fairfield
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. There has been a car in the Fairfield yard since every second Friday with a folding table on the passenger seat and no owner answering. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: the car and the plate together
I have to prove I tried before I can move it

quests.title: Storage Fees, Fairfield
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. Now that it is documented, Fairfield is owed $32 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: $32, from him or from the scrap
either way it comes off my floor

quests.title: First Year, Fairfield
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. I am in my first year at Fairfield and I have to log 39 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the supplier, two streets over
and get him a coffee, it helps
sign the book and I owe you

quests.title: The Air Line, Fairfield
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. Somebody has been coming into the Fairfield yard after half six to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: the ones who think the yard is public
the gate they are getting through

quests.title: My Own Car, Fairfield
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. My car has been at Fairfield since every second Friday and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $39. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: stand in the office where they can see you
the job card on the wall, all of it
now I know what I am arguing about

quests.title: The Assessor, Fairfield
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Fairfield works out of Carramar, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

steps.label: catch him before he goes out on the road
I want to hear how he does it

quests.title: Dumped Out the Back, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. People leave things at the Warrimoo roller door after knock-off and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: the pile, on a bad morning
the council will not act without one of these

quests.title: The Tip Fee, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. The photos worked, which means Warrimoo can claim back the $52 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since a public holiday nobody remembered. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: $52, and every receipt counts
I will do the form if you do the walking

quests.title: The Good Box, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: Before you say anything: yes, I know. Something came into Warrimoo on a public holiday nobody remembered in a box of paperbacks that I do not think the family meant to give away. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the address on the donation slip
the thing itself, before it goes back
I would rather give it back than sell it

quests.title: Sorting Room, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: It is not a police matter and I have checked. Two people have been coming into the Warrimoo sorting room since a public holiday nobody remembered and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

steps.label: catch them at the back door
$37, which is what the good stock made last month

quests.title: The Van, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. I do the Warrimoo pick-ups in a van with 37 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Do not let them talk you into anything.

steps.label: come out to Blaxland with me, it is a two-person lift
we will stop on the way, my shout

quests.title: Head Office, Warrimoo
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. Everything Warrimoo cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Blaxland, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. There's cash in it. Not a lot.

steps.label: turn up in person, that is the trick
tell me there is a person in there
